It tests whether Ollama's missing tool_choice and count_tokens cause tool-call failures or context-accounting error in Claude Code. It runs on CUDA on the 4090 and on Metal on the M5 Pro. Excluded from the Codex route, for three reasons: llama.cpp issue #24295 ('Responses API: silently drops namespace and web_search tool types → Codex CLI MCP tools unreachable') is OPEN, last updated 2026-09-16, and related issues #25193 and #23229 were closed NOT_PLANNED with no closing PR; the 10-02 receipt recorded a llama.cpp fork (PrismML) failing the function gate because 'the server skips the Codex client's namespace tool type'; and Codex has no built-in llama.cpp provider. The README itself says it makes 'no strong claims of compatibility with the Anthropic API spec' and that 'Tool use requires --jinja flag'.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The layer's model-choice axis has no qualified local route, and Ollama is the one local server both winners reach with no new credentials. Codex ships a first-party OSS provider for it: codex-rs/ollama at rust-v0.161.0 requires Ollama 0.13.4 or newer and builds the provider with WireApi::Responses, and cli/src/main.rs handles --oss and oss_provider. Claude Code reaches Ollama's Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434. The repository already holds a local integration check (evidence/artifacts/new-wsl-local-models-20261002/part-a-receipt.json). It ran Codex 0.160.0 through `codex exec --oss --local-provider ollama` and Claude Code 2.1.287 through `ollama launch claude` on Ollama 0.35.0: 10 of 10 simple client tasks per arm, recorded as not deciding, with the Anthropic surface exercised only by those tasks. Not yet established: (1) same-session resume on the local route; (2) the full MCP tool set; (3) failures caused by tool_choice, which Ollama does not support; (4) the token-count error, given that Ollama has no count_tokens endpoint, approximate token counts, no prompt caching, budget_tokens accepted but not enforced, and a /v1/responses that keeps no state; (5) macOS-arm64, where Ollama v0.40.0 runs MLX by default on Apple Silicon. Vendor boundary: code.claude.com says Anthropic does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through any gateway. The Claude Code arm is therefore a recorded model-choice route outside vendor support, and only the Codex arm is first-party. Pin drift: the stack installs v0.35.0 (adoption/new-wsl-profile.json L2595), while upstream v0.40.2 (2026-10-08) changed how `ollama launch claude` sets context length (#18855).
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run one preregistered paired trial on the RTX 4090 (WSL2) and on an M5 Pro. Controls: local models only (the slot holder swift-iq3s-s2o-64k, with gpt-oss:20b as control); no cloud models, no `ollama signin`, and Codex web_search="disabled". Pin the Ollama version and the client versions: Codex is pinned because rust-v0.162.0 removed the provider capability gate for tool namespaces (#50447), and Claude Code must be 2.1.285 or later so the Mac run can also test --desktop. Keep CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER the same in every arm, and use the manual environment-variable route (claude-code.mdx L194-196), not `ollama launch`. Reuse the retained resume and tool tasks (evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/native-clients/claude-resume-mcp-toolset.json and codex-resume-pinned-build.json, both present at repo HEAD 491aceef). Measure three things. (a) Resume: after the process is killed, does the same session or thread id continue with its prior context (claude --resume; codex resume or exec resume)? Pass or fail per run. (b) Tool-call failures per 100 calls, including whether MCP tools are reachable through the OSS provider. (c) Token-count error: client-reported usage (Claude Code stream-json usage or /context; Codex token_count events) against Ollama's own prompt_eval_count and eval_count. For Codex, also compare thread resume, tool events and token_count events with the OmniRoute cx/ route. The route qualifies as a model-choice route if resume passes on both hosts and tool-call failures and token-count error stay within preregistered bounds. It stays recorded and unqualified, as in the 10-02 receipt, if resume fails or failures exceed the bound. The 24 GB M5 Pro is an untested memory boundary: the 4090 run used 21,579 of 24,564 MiB with the embedder resident.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: Skill-efficacy measurement with paired arms in containers. 'bench skills eval' reads a skill's evals/evals.json, runs every case with and without the skill for each agent (claude-agent-acp, codex-acp) and reports the lift (docs/skill-eval.md). Promptfoo can also express paired arms on the host: two claude-agent-sdk providers, one with setting_sources ['project'] and skills: all and one without, using copy_working_dir. BenchFlow's verified differentiators are Docker-sandboxed arms with a lift table per agent, native SkillsBench tasks with deterministic verifiers, and subscription auth. It natively runs SkillsBench: 87 tasks across 8 domains with deterministic verifiers, matched no-Skills and curated-Skills conditions, an oracle that must pass first, and --sandbox docker for local runs. Those tasks are labeled independently of this stack, which addresses the gap-wave2 limit that the C9-C20 labels were written by the agent itself. It also supports Claude and ChatGPT subscription auth with no API key (native accounts), but the host's saved login is made available inside the sandbox, which is a credential-exposure cost. The discriminator against Harbor: skill-eval grading is an LLM judge over an expected_behavior rubric (0.0-1.0) or exact match on ground_truth (skill-eval.md lines 110-116), not a deterministic verifier; only the SkillsBench task runs use deterministic verifiers. Maintenance: 144 default-branch commits since 2026-07-11, and v0.7.8 on 2026-09-15. Not read: its telemetry and any nop control.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run one paired-skill experiment on a fixed SkillsBench subset with --sandbox docker, at least 3 repeats per arm, under three tools: BenchFlow, Harbor --skill and skill-creator's benchmark. Compare the lift estimates and their stddev, per-task agreement with the deterministic verifiers, and credential exposure (a subscription token inside the sandbox versus a gateway base URL). BenchFlow becomes the skill-evaluation lane if its lift matches the deterministic-verifier lift within run-to-run stddev and its failure artifacts can be inspected without a cloud sandbox. Otherwise Harbor with skill-creator's rule stays the reference.

The wave-2 receipt restored PostgreSQL only into a fresh PGDATA on the same machine and says independent-host restoration and host-loss recovery 'remain not_established and need hardware this task does not have'. The Mac application lane passed natively on one lived-in M5 Pro, and the installed apple/container 1.4.1 runs only Linux guests. Tart runs disposable macOS and Linux guests on the existing Apple Silicon Macs. Three verified features set it apart for a clean-OS restore and Mac-bootstrap acceptance: VM images are pushed to and pulled from any OCI registry, so a pinned base can be fixed by digest (README L7). A Packer plugin builds images (L8). --net-softnet gives stricter isolation in which the guest cannot reach the host (tart.run FAQ). Such a test needs no new hardware and sends no private research data to hosted CI runners. The gap is narrow. Restoring from the WSL2 workstation to a physical Mac is a stronger independent-host test, apple/container already gives a clean Linux guest, and Lume (trycua/cua, MIT, maintained) is already on trial in the platform layer for throwaway macOS VMs. So Tart is kept for a measured comparison, not targeted. candidates.demonstrated_gap: None for hosting. The README describes srt as 'a lightweight sandboxing tool for enforcing filesystem and network restrictions on arbitrary processes'. It is aimed at agents, local MCP servers and bash commands, and is labelled a 'Beta Research Preview' (README L3-9). It does not host long-running network services. On Linux 'the network namespace of the sandboxed process is removed entirely', and all traffic goes through host proxies over bind-mounted Unix sockets (L124). Seccomp blocks socket(AF_UNIX) creation by default (L943). allowLocalBinding defaults to false (L427). A FastAPI, Next.js or PostgreSQL listener inside srt would therefore not be reachable from host clients unless those defaults are weakened. That is an inference from the README; it was not executed. Supervision for this layer is already settled on systemd (open_gaps_followup index 4). The 2026-09-29 sweep already refuted srt on fit in the isolation layer, where it belongs. Decisive reason: role, not health. It is healthy: 211 default-branch commits since 2026-07-11, v0.0.79 on 2026-10-07, Apache-2.0.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: A defined requirement to confine one supporting service's egress and file writes under a single policy on both WSL2 and macOS. Under srt, with local binding or a Unix-socket path enabled, the FastAPI, Next.js and PostgreSQL fixture would have to keep passing its acceptance (12 pytest tests plus make verify) with host clients connected. Native systemd unit confinement on WSL2 would have to fail to express the same policy.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: Both M5 Pro hosts still lack a qualified local model route: every winner is 'untested' on macos-arm64. The 09-26 keep_but_compare was gated on v0.40.0 going stable, and that gate is now met: v0.40.0, v0.40.1 (2026-10-07) and v0.40.2 (2026-10-08) all have prerelease=false. The v0.40.0 notes say 'on Apple Silicon devices, model architectures supported by the MLX runtime will automatically run on MLX', with qwen3.8 (the control family) as the example. That puts an Apple-native engine behind the same CLI/API, with no separate MLX server. Two further gaps: (1) Ollama is the only packaged local runtime found for the new Cloudflare Clef/Clef-Flash decision models, which return per-option probabilities through POST /v1/systemone. The HF cards document only custom torch code tested in BF16 on an H200. Clef requires v0.35.1 or later, while the stack pins v0.35.0. (2) Local-only mode is documented: OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud, and a 127.0.0.1:11434 default bind. Costs: a daemon and a registry, plus v0.40.2's one-way model-store migration (backups kept; dropping below 0.40 needs a re-pull). Unverified: whether the Linux llama.cpp runner serves Clef on CUDA, and which quant the clef library tags ship. For generative arms on the 4090, Ollama 0.40 runs llama.cpp, which production already serves directly.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Bounded Mac trial at v0.40.2. On the 64 GB M5 Pro, run Qwen3.8-27B at about 4-bit three ways: Ollama (MLX default), mlx-lm (this sweep's round-1 arm, not re-proposed) and llama.cpp Metal llama-server. On the 24 GB host use the 9B tier, because li26's 27B Q4_K_M file alone is 16.46 GB. Use li26's frozen prompt.txt over a fixed subset of the 2020-03-02 8-K cohort, greedy with thinking disabled. Measure: prefill and decode t/s; peak unified memory, measured the same way in every arm; task-level output parity (micro-F1, JSON-valid rate and per-filing agreement with C0, since each engine's quant format differs); offline operation (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1, the log line 'Ollama cloud disabled: true', zero outbound connections with the network blocked after the pull); and restart recovery (time to the first valid reply after a launchd restart). Adopt Ollama for the Macs only if it is non-inferior on micro-F1 (li26 margin -0.02), within noise of the best arm on speed and memory, and passes offline and restart. Overturn it if llama.cpp Metal or mlx-lm matches it within noise, because Ollama adds a daemon, a registry and a store migration. Optional 4090 follow-up, under a new frozen plan: clef-flash or clef through /v1/systemone, with one noul question per 8-K item code, scored on micro-F1 against C0. li26's JSON-valid metric does not apply to that arm.

The unretained 09-26 idle probe nonetheless got device-level answers in WSL, so utilization under load is the untested boundary. Per-process fields cannot be compared through NVML on either side. This proposal deliberately replaces the critic's literal 'Windows-host exporter scraped by WSL Prometheus'. --nvidia-smi-command takes a full Windows path, so a second WSL-side instance can read nvidia-smi.exe through interop as the WDDM reference. That gives the same Windows reading without a Windows listener, and keeps both endpoints on loopback.

- --models-max, default 4 (:229)
- --models-autoload (:230)
- idle sleep via --sleep-idle-seconds (:244)
- per-model /metrics in router mode (:1122-1126)

Model swapping and idle release for the stack's only measured local engine therefore come from upstream once the pin moves from b11057 to v0.6.0, which is already-recorded drift. Router mode was verified at v0.6.0 only, not at the b11057 pin.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The requirement asks for custom tools through a supported SDK, and a named application needs them. The c4 worker's --lookup-tool flag (added 2026-09-23; blueprints/us-equities/workers/README.md:61-66, native_worker.py:257-258 at HEAD 491aceef) has to bypass the winner's typed SDK and send the raw dynamicTools field. This is still true at the newest upstream. At rust-v0.162.0 (openai-codex 0.162.0 on PyPI, 2026-10-08), AsyncCodex.thread_start has no tool argument (sdk/python/src/openai_codex/api.py:393-410; docs/api-reference.md:70). The protocol also marks the field #[experimental('thread/start.dynamicTools')] (codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs:145-151). Claude Agent SDK v0.2.165 documents what the winner lacks: typed in-process tools (@tool plus create_sdk_mcp_server, README.md:102-140), Python hook callbacks (README.md:199-246), a can_use_tool permission callback (types.py:2158), resume and fork_session (types.py:2040, 2249), and session_store. session_store mirrors transcripts to an external store, so resume can materialize when the local file is absent (types.py:2403-2410). That gives cross-host transcript resume between the WSL workstation and the Macs; it is not durable multi-host state or replay. Two things changed since the 2026-09-29 refutation: the named --lookup-tool application now exists, and the missing typed tool argument is verified at rust-v0.162.0. One measured weakness needs a retest. The stack's own interrupt receipt shows ResultMessage usage all zeros (terminal_reason aborted_streaming), and none of the 14 GitHub releases v0.2.151-v0.2.165 mentions interrupt usage. The two arms are billed differently: the Claude arm runs on API credits (seed note: 0.2.164 ran the 10-08 API-credit checks; the profile pins 0.2.163), while the Codex arm uses the native ChatGPT account. The trial is feasible on linux-wsl2-x86_64 now; macos-arm64 is untested.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run a re-preregistered matched rerun with a pinned judge. The 2026-10-03 decision says the layer-default verdict changes only through such a rerun (docs/decisions/2026-10-03-foundation-catalog-drift.md:103-106), and open gap 0 requires the pinned judge. Use the same c4 lookup-tool research tasks with N runs per arm. Arm A is openai-codex 0.162.0 (CodexClient with experimental dynamicTools). Arm B is claude-agent-sdk 0.2.165 (an in-process @tool server, deny-all except the tool). Measure: tool-call success, including parallel calls and tool-error returns; completeness of tool-call and tool-result events; usage completeness on interrupt against provider-side consumption; resume from a new process and from a second host (session_store against thread_resume); external effects; and cost normalized across API credits and the subscription. Decision rule: promote the Claude Agent SDK for custom-tool workers only if it matches or beats the Codex arm on tool success and event completeness without losing usage accounting. It is refuted for this role if the Codex typed SDK gains a non-experimental tool argument with equal results, or if Claude's interrupt usage stays zero while Codex reports it.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: This layer has never judged page-defined tools. Since v0.0.82 (2026-09-18), playwright-mcp offers the tools a page registers through WebMCP as `webmcp_<tool>`, on by default. They carry the page's own input schema and annotations, the list follows the current tab, and clients receive tools/list_changed. Upstream's own note says: 'Tool names, descriptions, schemas and results come from the page, so treat them as untrusted input'. Opt-outs are `--no-webmcp`, `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_WEBMCP=false` or config `webmcp: false` (README L438; 'Enabled by default' at L670). v0.0.83 bundles the same Playwright 1.64.0-alpha-1790635538000 as the stack's playwright-cli pin. By construction, these are unexamined tool entries entering the agent's MCP tool list. The WebMCP spec §6.3.1.1 names 'Metadata / Description Attacks (Tool Poisoning)' by malicious websites, and §6.3.2 warns that a tool's declared intent may not match its behavior. Stack winners already reach the same tools without MCP-native injection. playwright-cli 0.1.22 has `webmcp-list`/`webmcp-call` (since v0.1.20), and agent-browser has `webmcp list`/`webmcp invoke` (per SKILL.md at v0.38.2; the CLI command surface was not separately verified). playwright-mcp's only added capability is MCP-native exposure, with no measured advantage. candidates.demonstrated_gap: Codex's sign-in is a plaintext file wherever the stack runs it, although upstream supports an OS store. Executed on the WSL2 host on 2026-10-09 (HEAD 491aceef): `python3 scripts/credential_status.py --json` reports ${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/auth.json present, mode 0600, outside the worktree. config.toml has no cli_auth_credentials_store line, so the default applies; PR #49361's startup_preflight.rs comment says 'With file auth as the default'. Upstream offers file, keyring, auto and ephemeral. On macOS, keyring maps to the login Keychain (keyring-store Cargo.toml: apple-native), and a keyring save deletes the auth.json fallback (storage.rs). Claude Code and gh already default to the Keychain on macOS, so Codex is the one native sign-in there with an unused OS-store option. Two constraints were verified. (1) The WSL2 host has no Secret Service: org.freedesktop.secrets is neither owned nor activatable on the user bus. Codex's Linux backend is keyring 3.6 linux-native-async-persistent (keyutils plus Secret Service), so there 'keyring' fails and 'auto' falls back to auth.json. (2) The keyring entry is keyed per CODEX_HOME (compute_store_key(&self.codex_home)). tools/sota-convergence/codex_lane.py symlinks the native auth.json into isolated child CODEX_HOMEs (L522-523, L633), so it cannot work under keyring mode. The trial is therefore macOS-interactive only. rust-v0.160.0 (#49118) and rust-v0.161.0 (#49361, #49384) change docs, UI wording and storage-outcome telemetry, not the backend. Installed version: codex-cli 0.161.0.

(1) credential_status.py reports codex-native auth.json absent, plus a keychain record once an OS-store kind exists. (2) A `codex exec` smoke succeeds. (3) A token refresh after expiry works without a browser login. (4) No 'falling back to file storage' warning appears across sleep/wake and a locked-keychain SSH session. Keep file storage if any refresh or locked-keychain case fails, or if any tool on that host needs auth.json. WSL2 stays on file until a Secret Service passes the oo7 or gnome-keyring comparison and codex_lane.py no longer requires auth.json.

That is gh's plaintext fallback (cli/cli internal/config/config.go L418-434), used because this host has no Secret Service. GCM run as the Windows binary from WSL (docs/wsl.md L35-51, L111-118) keeps git's credential in the Windows host store; Windows Credential Manager is the default Windows store (credstores.md L31-35). Git for Windows' GCM is present at /mnt/c/Program Files/Git/mingw64/bin/git-credential-manager.exe (stat only; version unknown, not executed). The gap it closes is narrow. gh still needs its own token for gh api and PR work, so on WSL2 GCM leaves the plaintext hosts.yml token in place and adds a second stored GitHub credential. On macOS, gh (keyring first) and GCM (Keychain default) both use the login Keychain, so there is no gap. GCM has no default store on native Linux, and its Secret Service store requires a GUI session (credstores.md L17, L108). Credentials in the Windows store remain retrievable by any WSL process through interop (`git credential fill`), which the repository guard covers only by command text (secret_path_guard.py L1972-1982). candidates.demonstrated_gap: The WSL2 host has no Secret Service, measured 2026-10-09. The systemd user bus is up (DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS set), but org.freedesktop.secrets is neither owned nor activatable. secret-tool, gnome-keyring-daemon, oo7-daemon, kwallet and keepassxc are all absent. That is why gh fell back to plaintext hosts.yml, and why Codex keyring or auto cannot reach an OS store there. A Secret Service provider is the prerequisite for any OS-store kind for gh and Codex on WSL2. oo7 is a maintained Rust org.freedesktop.secrets server with PAM integration, a secret-tool replacement and a git-credential-libsecret replacement. The bridge-style alternatives found (crosskey, keyring_wincred, keyring-pybridge) are language-level libraries that neither gh's go-keyring nor Codex's keyring crate uses. Claude Code (Linux uses ~/.claude/.credentials.json only; its whole CHANGELOG has no keyring or libsecret line) and huggingface_hub (token file; no keyring support found in docs) would not move, so at most 2 of the 4 native sign-ins benefit. The README documents no headless or WSL unlock path; that, and WSL-distro packaging, are unverified. An empty-password or disk-stored unlock secret would be no better than today's 0600 files.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: On the WSL2 host, run oo7-daemon, with the distro's gnome-keyring as the comparison arm, owning org.freedesktop.secrets on the user bus. The operator unlocks it once per WSL boot with a secret that is not stored on disk. Pass requires five things. (1) gh auth login (keyring) and Codex keyring both persist across a full `wsl --shutdown` restart. (2) gh auth status reports token source 'keyring' and hosts.yml holds no token. (3) auth.json is absent. (4) Lanes keep working. (5) The collection is encrypted at rest. Not adopted if unlock needs a password on disk or a GUI, or if Codex auto silently falls back to file after a restart.

Facts come from the Codeberg API (repo, main commits, releases), Codeberg Cargo.toml and mergiraf.org docs. The GitHub API returns 404 for mergiraf/mergiraf. candidates.demonstrated_gap: The layer has no merge tool: difftastic only produces diffs. A read-only replay found 34 merges in this repository's history that git's default merge cannot complete. The replay used git 2.53.0 `merge-tree --write-tree` on all 100 two-parent merges on origin/main since 2026-09-01, which all fall between 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-22; 34 conflict under git's default ort merge. Thirty-three of the 34 contain a hunk where both sides changed the same entry's bytes and sha256 in the generated manifests/evidence.json. Those are true conflicts on derived data: no 3-way driver should resolve them, and the file should be regenerated instead. The population a merge driver can address is 65 conflicts across 24 merges in files other than the two generated ones: 43 JSON, 15 Markdown, 6 Python and 1 other. Mergiraf v0.20.0 supports the 49 JSON and Python conflicts but not Markdown. It can run after a conflict (`mergiraf solve`) or be enabled per repository through the untracked .git/info/attributes, so a trial changes no tracked config. `mergiraf review` gives an audit trail for every merge it solves. It is the current version of the comparator that weave's self-published table measures only at v0.16.3. There is no GitHub repository, so the canonical form here is the Codeberg URL.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run an offline replay in a scratch clone, on linux-wsl2-x86_64 and macos-arm64. Re-run all 100 recorded merges: the 34 that conflicted, plus the 66 clean ones as regression controls. Arm A is git ort. Arm B is mergiraf v0.20.0, registered only in the clone's local git config and .git/info/attributes; Git 2.44 or newer is recommended. Arm C is weave v0.5.4. Every arm regenerates the two generated files (manifests/evidence.json and docs/ecosystem/index.html) with the repository's own generators. Measure per file: clean resolutions; equality with the recorded merge tree, using canonical JSON equality for .json; wrong clean merges (clean but different from the recorded tree and failing scripts/validate.py or the tests); regressions on the 66 clean merges; and runtime. Adopt mergiraf, scoped to the extensions where it wins, only if it resolves more of the 49 JSON and Python conflicts than ort with zero wrong clean merges and zero regressions. Refute it if it resolves nothing beyond ort or produces any wrong clean merge.

candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20261009-api: Search direction from the completeness critic: GitButler was a metadata-only screen in 09-29. Sources are the GitHub API, README, crates/but listing, the gitbutlerapp/gitbutler-docs sources, docs.gitbutler.com, and a WebSearch for GitButler agent docs.
candidates.demonstrated_gap: GitButler has capabilities that worktrunk and plain git lack: an operation log with `but undo` and `but redo`; rebases that always succeed, marking commits as conflicted for later `but resolve`; several parallel and stacked branches in one working directory; and `but agent setup`, which installs a GitButler skill for Codex and Claude Code. As a replacement for worktrunk it does not fit this stack's lane model, for four documented reasons. First, GitButler's own docs advise worktrees 'when agents need incompatible checkout states, separate runtime state, or competing attempts', and every lane here runs validate.py and tests; the docs say parallel branches 'are not runtime isolation'. Second, workspace mode rejects a plain `git commit` on gitbutler/workspace, and every lane and script commits with git. Third, `but pr new` requires a GitButler forge account (`but config forge auth`), a new credential next to gh. Fourth, it defers conflicts rather than reducing them, while the measured conflicts sit in shared JSON manifests. No gap is demonstrated for the current requirement. It is a credible complement for independent small tasks in one checkout.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Use a disposable clone of this repository with two concurrent agent sessions, Claude Code and Codex, on independent tasks, plus one forced overlap in manifests/stack.json. Arm A uses worktrunk v0.80.0 with two worktrees and opens PRs with gh. Arm B uses `but` at release/0.22.3, or a pinned master commit, in one directory after `but setup` and `but agent setup`. It opens PRs with `but push` plus `gh pr create`, without GitButler forge auth. Measure on both hosts:
- correct branch attribution of every hunk
- conflicts surfaced, and the time to resolve them
- recovery from an injected bad rebase or amend (`but undo`/oplog against git reflog)
- interference between concurrent validate.py and test runs
- whether gh PR creation works
- the metrics setting
Move GitButler to targeted only if it matches correctness with zero cross-agent contamination and fewer manual steps, without a new credential.

counts.trading_layers_note: trading_layers counts only taxonomy layers with at least one selected entry, unlike foundation_layers (which counts every row); trading[] itself always has one row per taxonomy id, so len(manifest["trading"]) can exceed trading_layers whenever a taxonomy layer happens to have zero selected entries
counts.pin_status_note: pins_behind_upstream counts the generator's computed pin fields; pins_behind_upstream_by_review_status splits those rows by published review_status. A row's review_status is pin_behind_upstream[_unverified] only when its computed pin_behind_upstream is true, so review_status_pin_behind_upstream equals the pin_behind_upstream[_unverified] share of that split; a lane pin claim the computed fields contradict is published as pin_status_disputed[_unverified] (the lane's claim in disputed_lane_status and the row evidence) or, on an OS-package pin, distro_managed
counts.pins_behind_note: components with a commit-pinned version (a parenthetical hash), a non-GitHub repository, or an OS-distribution package pin (matched by an -Nubuntu/-Ndeb/+debN pin suffix, or by id via --os-package-ids, e.g. systemd even though its own repository is on GitHub) are excluded from the pin-vs-upstream comparison rather than counted either way
counts.pins_not_compared_note: rows whose pin the generator could not compare with upstream (the exclusions above, plus a pin or upstream latest with no parseable version, reason unversioned) carry pin_behind_upstream null and pin_comparison not_compared, never a definite false
counts.lane_groupings_note: every foundation/trading-scoped count above (candidates_total, candidates_by_disposition, components_confirmed, pins_behind_upstream, pins_behind_upstream_unique_components) is computed from all_rows = manifest['foundation'] + manifest['trading'] only, and so excludes lane_groupings[].selected rows the same way it excludes lane_groupings[].candidates; candidates inside lane_groupings (a review-lane grouping id outside the foundation/taxonomy baseline, e.g. an awesome-list survey) are counted only in lane_grouping_candidates; counts.citation_review (computed below, by apply_citation_review) is the same way scoped -- its rows_flagged/attached only ever count a foundation/trading row, never a lane_groupings[].selected row, since apply_citation_review only walks manifest['foundation'] and manifest['trading']
